news.headline: Partner uniQure submits BLA to FDA and MAA to UK MHRA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, delivered via ClearPoint's navigation platform
news.summary: uniQure submitted a Biologics License Application to the FDA requesting priority review, plus a Marketing Authorisation Application to the UK's MHRA, for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130), its Huntington's disease gene therapy, based on three-year Phase I/II data versus a propensity-matched Enroll-HD external control. Every dose in the trial was administered using ClearPoint's Navigation System and SmartFlow cannula, so the filing converts the long-pending Q3 BLA/MAA catalyst into an actual regulatory submission and starts the clock on the FDA's 60-day filing review.

news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro rallies 8.3% to $16.43 as the post-earnings selloff starts to reverse
news.summary: CLPT jumped 8.3% on August 25 from a $15.17 close to $16.43 on unusually thin volume of 179,361 shares, about 75% below the 719,603-share average, with no company announcement behind the move. Sell-side targets remain far above the market: B. Riley at $30, Lake Street at $25 and Stifel at $22 for a $25.67 consensus, while institutional ownership sits at roughly 30% of the float.

news.headline: MAK Capital group discloses 7.8% passive stake in ClearPoint Neuro via Schedule 13G/A
news.summary: MAK Capital Fund, MAK Capital One and Michael A. Kaufman jointly reported 2,375,861 CLPT shares (7.8% of shares outstanding) as of June 30 with shared voting and dispositive power, up from 6.3% disclosed earlier in the year. Filed nine days after the post-earnings selloff, the larger passive position points to institutional accumulation into the weakness, alongside BlackRock's 7.1% 13G from July 27.

news.headline: Stifel cuts price target to $22 and Lake Street to $25, both keeping Buy after the Q2 miss
news.summary: Stifel trimmed its target from $25 to $22 and Lake Street from $30 to $25, both maintaining Buy ratings after Q2 revenue of $10.9M came in roughly $1.8M below the $12.73M consensus and full-year guidance was cut about 7%. Shares fell another 16% in the August 4 session, taking the stock to roughly $13, less than half the $30.10 52-week high.

news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro reports Q2 2026 revenue of $10.9M (+18%), misses estimates and cuts FY guidance to $48-52M
news.summary: Q2 revenue rose 18% to $10.88M but landed about $1.8M below the $12.73M consensus, with neurosurgery navigation and therapy up 62% to $5.6M while biologics and drug delivery fell 15% to $4.0M on fewer products shipped to biopharma customers for new trial starts. Gross margin held at 62% but operating expenses jumped 51% to $17.0M, widening the operating loss to $10.2M and the net loss to $11.3M (adj. -$0.38 vs -$0.29 expected), cash fell to $29.4M from $45.9M at year-end, and FY2026 guidance was lowered from $52-56M to $48-52M.

news.headline: Investor deck lays out $500M long-term revenue target built on CAL, focused ultrasound and robotics
news.summary: Alongside the Q2 print management presented a five-pillar strategy targeting $500M in annual revenue, built on cell and gene therapy delivery to the brain, the newly possessed 30,000 sq ft ClearPoint Advanced Laboratories (CAL) site, the 10-year SONOCARE focused-ultrasound partnership at Sungkyunkwan University, a cranial robot shaped by feedback from 50+ neurosurgeons, and Harmony software. The deck cited 175+ active global centers, 60+ pharma partners, a 2.1 million-patient US opportunity across partner-targeted indications, and CAL lifting preclinical service capacity from roughly $8M to over $60M annually.

catalysts.label: uniQure presents four-year AMT-130 follow-up data
catalysts.detail: uniQure said it will present topline data from its ongoing Phase I/II AMT-130 studies in September 2026, covering all patients in the first two cohorts including four years of follow-up on 24 patients (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose) plus three additional high-dose patients at three years, measured on cUHDRS, TFC and other endpoints against a propensity-matched Enroll-HD natural-history control. Every one of those patients was dosed through ClearPoint's SmartFlow cannula and navigation system, so a clean four-year dataset following the September 2 BLA/MAA filing would further de-risk the regulatory review already underway. No exact date has been announced yet.

catalysts.label: FDA priority-review decision on uniQure's AMT-130 BLA (filing acceptance)
catalysts.detail: uniQure submitted the AMT-130 BLA on September 2, 2026 and requested priority review; the FDA typically rules on a priority-review request within 60 days of receiving a BLA, putting a decision around early November 2026. Priority review would compress the substantive review to roughly six months from acceptance, meaning a possible action date in Q2 2027; a standard-review outcome or a refuse-to-file letter would push the timeline out and is the main near-term risk to ClearPoint's most important partner program.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings: biologics back to growth and cash-burn check
catalysts.detail: ClearPoint has scheduled Q3 2026 results for November 5, 2026. Management said the CAL preclinical facility came into ClearPoint's possession in July and that new services revenue should return the biologics and drug delivery segment - down 15% to $4.0M in Q2 - to growth in Q3. The print is the first hard checkpoint on whether the cut to $48-52M was a genuine timing shift or a demand problem. With cash at $29.4M, opex up 51% year over year and an operating loss of $10.2M per quarter, investors will watch whether opex growth moderates or a capital raise moves onto the table.

catalysts.label: EpilepsyGTx EPY201 Phase 1/2a start
catalysts.detail: EpilepsyGTx plans a first-in-human Phase 1/2a trial of EPY201 for focal refractory epilepsy using ClearPoint's SmartFlow cannula and navigation system, with the company stating EPY201 enters first-in-human studies in 2026. Trial initiation would convert the mid-July partnership announcement into actual procedure and service revenue and add to the 10-15 trials management expects to be enrolling within 18 months.

catalysts.label: Aspen Neuroscience post-RMAT regulatory alignment
catalysts.detail: With RMAT designation granted on July 31 for sasineprocel (ANPD001), Aspen gains early and frequent FDA interactions and potential eligibility for accelerated approval for its autologous dopaminergic cell therapy in Parkinson's disease. An announced pivotal trial design or expanded ASPIRO enrollment would put a second approval pathway on ClearPoint hardware and lift procedure volumes ahead of any commercial launch.

catalysts.label: Further partner BLA filings flagged on the Q2 call
catalysts.detail: Management stated that multiple biopharma partners have recently received positive FDA feedback on potential BLA submissions and that additional cell and gene therapies should become commercially available by the end of 2027. Each partner filing beyond uniQure widens the base of recurring per-procedure delivery revenue and is the clearest way for ClearPoint to prove the platform thesis without depending on a single program.

catalysts.label: Partner trial ramp and roughly 10 data readouts
catalysts.detail: Management guided on the Q2 call to 10-15 clinical trials using ClearPoint technology enrolling patients over the next 18 months, plus roughly 10 partner data readouts. This is the core driver of the biologics and drug-delivery revenue line and the main evidence needed to support the $500M long-term revenue ambition.

catalysts.label: First GLP IND-enabling study completed at CAL; robotics prototypes in preclinical use
catalysts.detail: ClearPoint signed its first GLP statement of work for the CAL facility, targeted for completion in 2027, and expects functioning cranial robot prototypes to be used preclinically at CAL and to generate incremental service revenue in 2027. Delivering both would prove out the capacity expansion from roughly $8M to over $60M in annual preclinical service capacity that underpins the new strategy.

catalysts.label: Potential FDA decision on AMT-130
catalysts.detail: With the BLA filed September 2, 2026 under a priority-review request, an FDA action date would fall roughly six months after acceptance, pointing to Q2 2027 (potentially April-May) if priority review is granted; a standard-review clock would push this later. Approval would establish recurring per-procedure delivery revenue for ClearPoint and be the first commercial validation of the platform in a large chronic indication, following the Kebilidi precedent where SmartFlow is the only FDA-authorized delivery device.

pulse: The headline development remains partner uniQure's September 2 submission of the AMT-130 BLA to the FDA (with a priority-review request) plus a parallel MAA to the UK MHRA, converting the single most important pending catalyst in the CLPT thesis from a guided plan into an actual filing built entirely on ClearPoint's navigation system and SmartFlow cannula. Rather than sustaining a rally, CLPT has faded since: after the August 25 spike to $16.43, shares drifted back to $14.90 on September 1, $14.31 on September 2 and roughly $14.00-14.24 through September 3-4, suggesting the filing itself was largely anticipated and priced in, with the stock still well below the $30.10 52-week high and sell-side targets (B. Riley $30, Lake Street $25, Stifel $22, consensus ~$25.67). No new CLPT-specific operational or financial news has emerged since the August 3 Q2 report (revenue of $10.88M missed estimates, biologics and drug delivery fell 15%, opex rose 51%, cash dropped to $29.4M, FY2026 guidance cut to $48-52M), while MAK Capital (7.8%) and BlackRock (7.1%) built stakes into the earlier weakness. The next real checkpoints are uniQure's promised September four-year AMT-130 follow-up data, the FDA's roughly 60-day filing-acceptance/priority-review decision expected around early November, and ClearPoint's own Q3 print now confirmed for November 5, where biologics needs to reaccelerate on the new CAL facility or the shrinking cash runway becomes the dominant story.
